mechanism: Three open revision holders expose the independently held reader copy alongside the authoritative source and cache. Publication and deletion change source/cache without changing the held token; filling later copies that token into the cache.
spatialBenefit: None substantive. The race ordering is real depth beyond the video (which assumes no concurrent writes), but it is temporal. The scene is three holders showing a digit; their arrangement in space encodes nothing a three-cell table would not, and orbiting reveals nothing.
beyondVideoTest: Ordering counterfactual passes (publish during a suspended read leaves source 2, held 1, cache empty; late fill restores 1). Spatial test fails: no viewpoint, cut or boundary change adds information.
interaction: Read source / Fill from held copy / Read cached revision; Publish 2 + delete key becomes repeatable Delete cached key. All changes are immediate, never playback; host Reset restores the overview.
expectedObservations: Read, publish, finish: the delete finds an empty cubby, then the late fill puts revision 1 in the cache while the archive holds revision 2; a later hit returns revision 1.
Publish, read, finish: the reader copies revision 2 and the cache matches the source.
Read, finish, publish: the delete removes the cached revision 1 and the next miss reads revision 2.
A hit never moves anything through the tunnel: the source is not read.
sourceGuide: content/concepts/cache-aside.json (overview, walkthrough step 4, exercise 'Make a stale runbook visible')
limitations: No expiry, authorization or leases modelled.
Recommend omission from 3D; the ordering counterfactual would suit a small 2D interactive or the guide exercise.
